items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: The reason I am writing all these details is that I want you and Lord Donegal to deal with each other directly, and I don't want to become involved as a third party.

ctx.x: Now, I just showed you the kind of propaganda that the people put out. They all knew about Tiger Rag. Now, here's a Negro. I'm going to give you his record. And if I'm wrong, then the world is wrong. This Negro lived in Plaquemine, Louisiana, at the age of about six to eight years old, worked as a shoeshine boy for Ferdinand Herbert, who operated a barbershop in Plaquemine, Louisiana. He came to New Orleans in his late teens. He lies as to hearing Buddy Bowling play. From the dates given in the second line of…

No. It's going now. This is a letter. At the head is Dr. Admiral Sushaw, New Orleans. They, December 29, 1949. Dear Mr. LaRock, resuming our conversation of last night, I would simply write to repeat. The Marcus of Donegal wrote me and asked me to communicate to you. His address is, the Marcus of Donegal, 16 High Park Gate, London, SWF, England. As you know, Lord Donegal is head of all the jazz clubs of Great Britain. They're planning to have a 30-year centennial commemorating the opening up of the original Dixie…

Well, that'll go to show you how a man can speak out of both sides of his mouth. I received a letter. Now, there's been plenty going on after Marshall Steins had given Tom Brown this favorable write-up. Brown was to go to different papers and have this printed and show it as real history. This was lying history connived by this man, Marshall Steins, who somewhere along in the front of these reels, you'll read his letter that he admitted to me he was lying.
